explanation: Each row is two counted loops -- one printing leading spaces, one printing stars -- followed by a bare println() to end the line. Writing the two counts as formulas of the row index (size - 1 - i spaces, 2 * i + 1 stars) keeps both halves consistent. The bottom half reuses the same row formula with the index counting back down from size - 2, which is what stops the widest row from being printed twice.
hints: Use System.out.print inside the loops (no line break) and one System.out.println() at the end of each row.
Factor the row into a small private helper that takes size and i; then the bottom half is just the same helper called with i counting down.
The bottom half starts at i = size - 2, not size - 1, otherwise the middle row repeats. A loop that starts below 0 never runs, which handles size 0 and negatives for free.
